target_customer: SaaS and web app users who get stuck and pay an expert by the minute over screenshare
problem: Users hit snags in tools like Squarespace, Mixpanel and Mailchimp and cannot get fast expert help; Sixty let them summon an expert in minutes.
business_model: Managed marketplace charging per minute, starting at 1 dollar per minute per the YC page

founders.name: David Head
founders.background_notes: YC page bio only. The YC launch post names no founders.

competitors.name: Codementor
competitors.what: On demand one on one developer help marketplace with screen sharing, sessions billed in short increments

technical_complexity.rationale: Matching and screenshare sessions can be built on existing video tools; the YC launch post claims 1,500 problems solved across 70 apps, so the hard part was operations.

defensibility.rationale: Marketplace of freelancers, copyable by Codementor and general freelancer sites; no source shows exclusive supply or lock in.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Sixty; the company is marked Inactive and the usesixty.com site returned 404.

market_need_then: The YC launch post of 2017-07-21 claimed over 1,500 problems solved on 70 web apps and customers including Grammy nominated production agencies and other YC startups, which is self reported.

branding.domain_note: Used usesixty.com, a use prefix, rather than an exact match domain; a later unrelated Sixty AI product also exists.
branding.community_and_virality: A Bubble forum post celebrated the company, built on Bubble, getting into YC (search result title).

brand_strength.rationale: The name hints at per minute pricing but is a common word, and a later unrelated Sixty AI product takes the same name.

outcome_analysis: Sixty was a managed per minute expert help marketplace in YC Summer 2017 that claimed early usage in its launch post. It is marked Inactive by YC and its website returns 404, but no shutdown notice, post-mortem or funding history was found, so the cause is not public and failure factors are left empty.
notes: Two funding searches found nothing for this company. Codementor is dated 2014, within a few years before the batch; the TechCrunch URL was seen only in search results. The YC page lists a founding year of 2015 and team size of 4 but names one founder. usesixty.com returned 404. Outcome search found no cause.
